name: Greyish Teal
lede: Greyish Teal is a soft, desaturated blue-green that our painting archive finds far more often than most crowd-survey colors, especially in Matisse and Klimt.

sections.title: A modifier, and a Japanese near-twin
sections.body:
The 2010 xkcd color survey carries this name, and our library separately holds a Japanese traditional color, *Mizu'asagi* (水浅葱), that lands close to the same hue; its kanji read literally as "pale green onion" [1]. The two names were coined independently, by different systems centuries apart, and we hold no evidence either influenced the other [1].

ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the swatch as a light bluish green, and the nearest library neighbor is [[dull-teal|Dull Teal]] [2]. It sits as a muted, greyed-down [[teal|teal]], paler and softer than the saturated web color of the same family name [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, carries this color in 81 paintings at five percent coverage or more[3]. The strongest single match is Claude Monet's 1904 [[painting:nga-61377|Waterloo Bridge, London, at Dusk]], where it covers about 60 percent of the canvas [3]. Henri Matisse carries it at nearly thirty times the archive's overall rate across his dated works, and Gustav Klimt at over seventeen times that rate [3]. In the paintings that hold it, this color sits as a highlight three times out of five, more often than as a shadow [3]. It also shares canvases with [[viridian|Viridian]] and [[sage|Sage]] far more than chance would predict [3].
